rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and 3 (Figs. 5-11): the authors report their own airborne hyperspectral and thermal campaigns over 27 olive orchards in Spain and Italy (2011-2017), field disease-severity assessments of thousands of trees, and a three-stage random-forest/spectral-clustering method whose sensitivity and specificity results are reported (e.g., OA 98% and kappa 0.7 for Vd, OA 92% and kappa 0.8 for Xf).
rows.notes: The study is primary but it only shows that airborne hyperspectral/thermal traits can detect Xf- and Vd-infected olive trees and discriminate the two pathogens from each other and from water stress. It reports no result on controlling or limiting Xf expansion (the 'challenge' the passage refers to, function pest_control). Eradication/control is mentioned only as a motivation in the Introduction and as a future benefit in the Discussion, not as a measured outcome. Detection is a precondition of control, so Q2 is 'no' and upstream is set. Note the study is not about early/pre-visual detection either: it classifies trees with DS>=1 (visible symptoms) and explicitly lists early-stage detection as future work. Q3-Q9 therefore 'no' by rule.

notes: Full text appears complete (Introduction through References). Supplementary Table S1 (index list) not included but not needed for the rating.
